title: Hanuman in disguise
hookLine: a frightened king, two strangers with bows, and a careful messenger
carry: hanuman calms the fear, then finds the truth

cards: Spring at Lake Pampa. Lotuses, bees, birds calling, trees heavy with flowers. And Rama, standing at the shore, finds it unbearable.
The Kishkindha Kanda opens on a man surrounded by beauty, and every bit of it reminds him of the person who isn't there.
He talks to his brother about it at length, the flowers, the breeze, the birds, and none of it helps. Lakshmana listens for a long time. Then he says, gently, enough.
Grief like this will wear you down. Let's go.

teach.b: Up on a mountain called Rishyamuka, someone is watching. Sugriva, the exiled monkey prince, sits there with four counselors.

He sees two men with bows walking straight toward his hiding place, and he panics: his brother Vali must have sent them to kill him. Sugriva turns to his wisest counselor, Hanuman, who calms him first.
You're jumping at shadows, he tells him, more or less, and a king who acts on fear before he knows is a weak king.
Then Sugriva gives him the job: go down, find out who they are, watch their faces and their speech, tell me if they mean harm. And Hanuman doesn't go as a monkey.
He takes the form of a wandering mendicant, a bhikshu. Days ago in the story, Ravana came to Sita disguised as a holy man, to deceive and to steal.
Now Hanuman takes nearly the same disguise, to find out the truth and to protect.

Same costume, opposite hearts. This first scene is the Hanuman Hindus pray to. Before he leaps the sea, he's the one who steadies a frightened friend and walks toward the thing everyone's afraid of, to look.

Devotees call him Sankat Mochan, the remover of troubles. Many recite the Hanuman Chalisa, a much later hymn whose name means forty, when they're afraid: before an exam, on a dark road, in a hospital waiting room.
The one they call on is this one: calm when others panic, and brave enough to go and see.

how: Hanuman is worshiped as Sankat Mochan, remover of troubles: many devotees recite the Hanuman Chalisa when afraid and visit his temples on Tuesdays and Saturdays. In Valmiki he first appears here, as Sugriva's counselor.

o: a monkey counselor who serves an exiled prince
a wandering mendicant, the form Hanuman takes
a royal messenger who carries a king's sealed letter

games.q: the first scene of Kishkindha — tap the pairs.

s: Sugriva welcomes the strangers right away
he panics, sure that Vali has sent them to kill him.
he takes the form of a wandering mendicant.
in Valmiki, we first meet Hanuman leaping the sea
we first meet him calming Sugriva's fear and going down the mountain to find out the truth.

games.q: your little brother can't sleep: he's scared of the dark, and Nani's away. what's a Hindu thing you could do with him?
o: tell him fear is silly and turn off the light.
say Hanuman's name with him, the one who calms fear.
let him stay up until he's too tired to care.
games.why: the first time we meet Hanuman, he calms a frightened king; Hindus call on him as Sankat Mochan when they're afraid.

practice: Think of something that's been making you anxious. When fear comes, many Hindus simply say Hanuman's name. Breathe in; on the out breath, say softly, jai Hanuman.
If you don't pray, say instead: pause, then look. Do it a few times, and let the fear make room for one clear next step, the way Hanuman calmed Sugriva before he went down the mountain.

wordCard.voice: Bhikshu, a wandering mendicant: the form Hanuman takes to go find out who the two armed strangers are.

orig.note: Sanskrit pampā: the lake where the Kishkindha Kanda opens, traditionally placed near Hampi in Karnataka.
